A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Three-view Focal Length Recovery From Homographies. All 14 pages, including supplementary Sections 8–11, are readable and support comparison of the text, equations, figures and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments and real-world focal-length evaluations in Section 6 and supplementary Section 10, including Figures 2–4 and 6 and Tables 2–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original synthetic and real-world experimental results, including the supplementary evaluations for Cases III and IV.

M1.justification: The four focal-length solvers, elimination constraints, Sturm-sequence and hidden-variable procedures, and LO-RANSAC estimation with P3P and nonlinear refinement are unchanged in Sections 4–5 and supplementary Sections 8–9.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four camera configurations, synthetic planar and dominant-plane scenarios, six-scene real-world dataset, and Book scene modified with off-plane objects. Supplementary coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within each experiment: Table 2 retains the same fEf, fEf + PP and Ef variants, and Tables 3–4 retain the same P4Pf-based comparators. The Heikkilä comparison in Table 1 also matches.

E3.justification: Synthetic sampling, image-triplet counts, evaluation metrics, RANSAC budgets and thresholds are unchanged. Both versions retain the supplementary protocols disabling local optimization for Figure 6 and applying field-of-view filtering in Table 3.

E4.justification: The numerical-stability, noise, planarity and known-focal-length sensitivity analyses are identical. The speed–accuracy study and supplementary field-of-view filtering and off-plane-object analyses are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same distribution plots and boxplots in Figures 2, 3 and 6. There are no changes to run or seed disclosures, uncertainty estimation, confidence intervals or significance testing.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results, plotted data and qualitative findings match throughout the main paper and supplement. For example, Table 2 retains the Case I Hfff + P3P median focal-length error of 0.0439 and runtime of 49.31 ms.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, normal-consistency constraints, elimination derivations, solution counts and equations (1)–(29) are unchanged, including the supplementary derivation and Case IV solver.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims concerning novel constraints, four efficient solvers, comparative accuracy and efficiency, and the planar-scene dataset. No contribution is added, removed or redefined.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same pure-translation degeneracy discussion, multiple-solution limitations for Cases III/IV, and explanations of how off-plane points and focal-length priors help resolve ambiguity in Sections 6.2 and 10.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information matches, including PoseLib, the supplementary Macaulay2 code, hardware, calibration procedure, SuperPoint/LightGlue matching details, and code/data access and release statements.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, positioning relative to Heikkilä and other two-view and three-view methods, and all 46 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 13 Jan 2025 to v2 dated 6 Nov 2025. The paper's prose, headings, terminology and section order, including the supplement, are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–5 retain the same graphics, labels, captions, structure and placement. Page layout is unchanged; the small rendering differences involve negligible glyph-position shifts.

improvement.justification: The main paper and supplement preserve the same methods, theory, evidence, limitations and reproducibility information. The version/date-stamp update and negligible rendering differences provide no meaningful overall quality improvement or deterioration.
